column1: # Game profile of Super Mario Party Jamboree (Switch, update 2.3.0). Plays on the Mac
# NintendoWare Bezel Engine 2.9, SDK 17.5.9: nearly all of RomFS is in Bezel Engine archives (.bea, the 2.9 form with inline entries; zstd entries); the shaders are BNSH in their
# .fshb / .bfsha / .bnsh entries and in main (shader_split.py bea_members). The minigames, boards and modes are 139 NROs (nro/NX_Release, one NRR), loaded with ro::LoadModule

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so on the Switch IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true. nninitStartup (main+0x98281c, Big Brain Academy's form) chooses its memory setup
# by it: with virtual address memory, malloc's StandardAllocator gets a 2 GB address region and Bezel's a 56 GB one; without, it sets a heap of pool − used memory, malloc gets 32 MB
# of it and Bezel the rest. The 4.375 GB alias region of the 5 GB block leaves Bezel 2.06 GB beside malloc's idle 2 GB (5 MB mapped), and Bezel needs more: with a 64 GB alias region
# it held 2.3 GB at the Party Plaza; with 2.06 GB it returned null for a 46 MB request as the plaza loaded (main+0x8d9a48). Both regions need about 5.2 GB of alias region, more than
# a phone without extended addressing gives with Metal beside it, so the profile reports no system resource and the game takes its heap path: a 3.14 GB heap in the 4 GB layout
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; BNSH in the Bezel Engine archives, bea_members) ----
# the NVN depth mode the game sets (nvnDeviceSetDepthMode near = 0): the prebuilt pipeline bases take the main0_z vertex entries
